posts.title: Why Success Doesn't Make You Happy
posts.description: William von Hippel on psyche.co has a theory about why we're less happy than hunter-gatherers despite having everything: we evolved with two competing needs. Connection and autonomy. Both make us happy. Both must be balanced. Connection kept our ancestors alive. Autonomy made them valuable to the group. posts.title: The Shoe Store Time Capsule
posts.description: Messy Nessy Chic dug up this surreal story: a shoe store closed for 40+ years. Behind dusty windows sat a fashion museum from the 1940s-60s. Tartan saddle shoes. Art deco boxes. Converse before sneakers. A vintage costume company bought some. The rest is still there. Location isn't public. Some secrets should stay secret. Great read! The Forgotten Family Shoe Store — via Messy Nessy Chic

posts.title: Reels as Relationship Maintenance
posts.description: Shanna Tiayon from Greater Good Magazine wrote something that made me feel less bad about my Instagram habits. Her thesis: sending reels isn't mindless scrolling. It's relationship maintenance. She and her best friend of 25 years live far apart, both busy with careers and kids. Email became impossible. Phone calls rarely happen. So they send reels.
